# Widi Ginanjar

> Runs community programs and the applied research around them, mostly on sustainability, in Indonesia. Also does SEO consulting for NGOs, B2B firms, hospitality brands, and organisations navigating AI search, and writes field notes and essays in Bahasa Indonesia. Background in community-based development (Delterra, YCAB, BIDUK) and in SEO and growth marketing (BetterPic, Runflow).

## Essays (field notes and essays, in Bahasa Indonesia)

- [Essays index](https://widiginanjar.com/writing/): All essays and field notes.
- [Tutur Nenek (English: My Grandmother's Stories)](https://widiginanjar.com/writing/tutur-nenek.html): Reading Anne-Lot Hoek's Merebut Bali reminded me of my grandmother's stories about the Dutch and Japanese eras in Ponorogo, East Java. Indonesian: Membaca Merebut Bali karya Anne-Lot Hoek membuatku teringat Mbah, dan ceritanya tentang zaman Belanda dan Jepang di Ponorogo.
- [Dulu Ada yang Meminta Air (English: Once, Someone Asked for Water)](https://widiginanjar.com/writing/dulu-ada-yang-meminta-air.html): Field notes from a village in Bangli, Bali: a long dry season, water trucks at Rp250,000 each, an 80-metre borehole with no water, and a local legend of a water curse. Indonesian: Catatan lapangan soal kekeringan di Bangli: air tangki Rp250 ribu per truk, sumur bor 80 meter tanpa air, dan legenda kutukan air dekat Danau Batur.
- [Yang Bergairah di Landih (English: What Thrives in Landih)](https://widiginanjar.com/writing/yang-bergairah-di-landih.html): In Landih, Bangli, coffee and citrus are thriving, while bamboo is pushed to the slopes and riverbanks. Indonesian: Di Landih, Bangli, kopi dan jeruk tampak bergairah, sementara bambu terdesak ke lereng dan tepi sungai.
- [Meditasi adalah: Sebuah jebakan betmen (English: Meditation Is a Sneaky Trap)](https://widiginanjar.com/writing/meditasi-vipassana.html): Ten days of silent Vipassana retreat in Bogor, and an answer to people who ask why I went. Indonesian: Cerita 10 hari silent retreat Vipassana di Bogor, dan jawaban untuk pertanyaan orang soal kenapa aku ikut.

## Services

- [Services overview](https://widiginanjar.com/services/): SEO consulting: services and booking.
- [SEO for NGOs & Mission-Driven Teams](https://widiginanjar.com/services/ngo.html): Technical SEO for NGOs, nonprofits, and social enterprises.
- [B2B SEO Strategy for Professional Services](https://widiginanjar.com/services/b2b.html): SEO and backlink strategy for consulting, research, and B2B firms.
- [Restaurant SEO in Bali for Hospitality & F&B Brands](https://widiginanjar.com/services/hospitality.html): Local SEO and Google Business Profile optimisation for restaurants, bars, and hospitality groups.
- [AI Search Optimization & Citability](https://widiginanjar.com/services/ai-search-era.html): Helping organisations get found and accurately cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI summaries.
- [Konsultan SEO di Bali untuk Hotel, Restoran, dan Yayasan](https://widiginanjar.com/services/konsultan-seo-bali.html): SEO services in Bahasa Indonesia for hotels, villas, restaurants, and foundations in Bali.
- [About](https://widiginanjar.com/about.html): Background, approach, and career history.

## Notes (technical write-ups and case studies)

- [Notes index](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/): Full archive of write-ups on SEO, growth, and AI search.
- [Domain Rating 5 to 38 in Under Two Months, With Zero Paid Links](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/dr-5-to-38-zero-paid-links.html): How relationship-based outreach moved an AI product's Domain Rating from 5 to 38 in under two months, and what that number doesn't prove.
- [Anyone Can Be an SEO Specialist Now. So What Am I Actually Selling?](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/what-am-i-actually-selling.html): Anyone can list what's broken on a page now. Here's what that leaves for a human SEO consultant to actually be paid for.
- [Being Right About the Data Isn't the Same as Being Responsible With It](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/being-right-vs-being-responsible-ngo-comms.html): A social post about forest fires led to a disagreement over one closing line. Sorting out why took longer than writing the post did.
- [Google Knows My Website. It Doesn't Know Me.](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/ai-overview-domain-vs-name.html): Two searches, minutes apart. One found my site accurately. The other pulled from LinkedIn and mixed me up with someone else entirely.
- [The Small Grey Text Under a Google Result That Most People Skip](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/google-missing-word-serp-snippet.html): A page ranking #1 was still getting a below-average click rate. The reason was sitting in plain sight, in small grey text most people scroll straight past.
- [I Didn't Know What 'Carbon Offset' Meant Until Last Year](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/sustainability-jargon-carbon-offset-sdgs.html): I worked in sustainability for years and still didn't understand carbon offset until last year. Most people don't either.
- [Getting an Issue Found Isn't Always About Search](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/fundraiser-map-peer-sharing-vs-search.html): Search only finds people who already know what to look for. A nonprofit fundraiser built as a map shows another route in, through people's own networks.
- [Nonprofit SEO Isn't Business SEO, Because the Audiences Don't Want the Same Thing](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/nonprofit-seo-three-audiences.html): A business site can point every visitor at one outcome. A nonprofit site can't. Two real homepages show what happens when a site serves only one audience.
- [The Insider Test: If People in Your Own Sector Can't Explain Your Work, Nobody Else Can](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/insider-test-curse-of-knowledge-ngo.html): Even people at other NGOs couldn't say what the NGO I worked for actually did. That's the curse of knowledge, and it explains most nonprofit jargon.
- [I Checked 15 Organizations' Traffic. Only One Had Meaningful Paid Search.](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/15-organizations-paid-traffic-pattern.html): A curiosity-driven check across NGOs and companies of every size found the same pattern almost everywhere, and one outlier that didn't fit any theory I had.
- [You Can DIY Half of This. Here's the Half You Can't.](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/diy-half-of-seo.html): AI can spot a missing meta description in seconds. It can't tell you which broken thing is actually urgent versus which one just looks urgent.
- [What Reviewing AI Responses Taught Me About Writing for Search](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/reviewing-ai-responses-writing-for-search.html): A pattern from reviewing AI model responses for accuracy, and what it means for writing content AI systems can quote correctly.
- [Your Impact Report is a PDF. Search Engines Barely See It.](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/pdf-invisible-to-search.html): A well-designed PDF impact report can still be nearly invisible to search engines and AI. Here's why, and what a simple structure change fixes.
- [The SEO Checklist for NGOs With No Marketing Team](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/seo-checklist-ngo-no-marketing-team.html): A practical checklist for the person wearing five hats at a small NGO, written for someone with no SEO background and limited time.
- [Instagram Scores 100 on Authority. The Cafe Down the Street Scores 9](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/instagram-scores-100-cafe-scores-9.html): Three things one small audit turned up, the kind that actually change what you do next, not just interesting trivia.
- [I Rank #2 on Google for My Own Name. AI Still Doesn't Know I Exist.](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/ranking-vs-ai-citation.html): A live test of AI-citability with the easiest keyword there is, my own name. Ranking on Google turned out to be a different problem from being cited by AI.
- [Why My Portfolio's Domain Is My Name, Not "Bali SEO"](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/why-my-domain-is-my-name.html): A friend asked why I didn't buy a keyword-matching domain instead. The answer says something about how AI search is changing what actually gets rewarded.
- [My SEO Portfolio's Title Tag Said "Notion" for Two Weeks](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/my-own-title-tag-said-notion.html): I built a portfolio to sell SEO audits. Its own title tag was generic platform branding the whole time. A lesson in checking your own site first.
- [Grantmakers Check Your NGO Website Before Your Impact Report](https://widiginanjar.com/notes/grantmakers-check-your-website-first.html): Before a funder reads your proposal, they look at your website. How one canonical tag error cost a real membership network its search visibility.
